taxonomy.note: Current Kew/POWO accepts Solidago radula and lists Texas in its native range.

target_zone_range.evidence_basis: Burnet — UT PRC Vascular Plants of Burnet County provides a field-based Solidago radula treatment. Travis — UT PRC Travis County herbarium specimen index includes Solidago radula. Williamson — UT PRC Studies on the Vascular Plants of Williamson County includes Solidago radula.
target_zone_range.guardrail: Use exact county floristic/herbarium evidence; do not infer a county from a city/locality label when the county is not explicitly supplied.

morphology.look_here_first: Touch and inspect the stem and leaves first: rough goldenrod is genuinely scabrous, with short stiff jointed hairs on the stem and rough leaf surfaces. Then compare the broader lower leaves, rapid reduction upward, and the compact terminal panicle before looking at tiny head details.
best_field_traits: erect to ascending rhizomatous perennial, often 1–3 stems
stem conspicuously rough/hispid with stiff short hairs
foliage distinctly scabrous to the touch
lower leaves oblanceolate to ovate and larger; upper leaves abruptly smaller
terminal compact paniclelike array of many small yellow heads
calcareous rocky openings, prairies and dry woods
morphology.key_separation: S. radula is the rough/scabrous one: stiff stem and leaf hairs are more tactile and obvious than the fine gray pubescence of S. nemoralis. Its flowering array is generally more compact and terminal rather than the strongly one-sided wandlike pattern typical of S. nemoralis.
